principles.text: Validation is people paying, not free users, usage or compliments. Revenue is the only metric for whether to continue.
Ship a new product every week and drop what earns nothing in two weeks; expect a 10% success rate at best.
Price in the $40-$100/month band. Raising Tweet Hunter from $9 to $49 lowered churn while revenue went up.
Don't scale acquisition before retention. Once users stick, go all in on the one or two channels that work.
As AI pushes build costs toward zero, value shifts to distribution: SEO, creator partnerships, an owned audience.

sampleQA.question: How do I know if my SaaS idea is validated?

answer.text: Only payments count. Free users and usage only prove people will use it for nothing.
Build a one-feature MVP, promote it, track payments for two weeks. No payment means a new idea.
Strong later signals: people paying again in month two, and signups arriving on days you do no promotion.

sampleQA.question: What should I charge for a B2B SaaS?

answer.text: Pick a band of $40-$100/month and don't revisit it before $100k MRR unless nobody buys or everyone churns.
Tweet Hunter went $9 to $49 over about 12 months; churn went down, because price filters who signs up.
Keep one plan with no credits or tiers, like Outrank at $99/month for 30 articles.
Require a credit card for trials: 100 serious trials beat 1,000 sign-ups who ghost.

sampleQA.question: How did Tweet Hunter get its early growth?

answer.text: Gave a Twitter influencer 25% of monthly profit in exchange for owning marketing and promotion.
That launch took MRR from about $3K to $20K in two weeks.
Support went to Tibo's own DMs; fixing bugs in minutes got users tweeting about it.
Free SEO mini tools, more than one a month (about 40 total), became most of the traffic.
